Confidence floor, accept side. Measured edit distance 1 against 'pune'; observed confidence 0.8833333333333334, above the floor, so the correction is applied. Confidence floor, reject side. Measured edit distance 1 against 'pune' - the same distance as TC-76 - yet observed FLAGGED with UNMATCHED. Because the distance cap cannot explain this rejection, only the confidence floor can, this is the one row that fails if the floor is lowered or deleted. Every other flagged row is rejected by distance and would survive that change.

Long-name distance cap, accept side. Measured edit distance 2 against 'bangalore' (length 9, so the cap is 2); observed confidence 0.9555555555555556. Sits exactly on the cap rather than inside it, so narrowing the cap to 1 turns this row red.

Long-name distance cap, reject side at measured edit distance 3. The remediation table proposed 'Bangaloreee' for this row on the assumption it was distance 3; it was measured at distance 2 and observed ENRICHED to Bangalore with confidence 0.9636363636363636, so the input was corrected to one more 'e'. The observation won over the assumption, which is the point of measuring every boundary row before committing it.
